findings.text: The lane provides single register read and write dispatchers that validate the high architecture class of the caller supplied identifier and then route by category toward core, firmware, scalable vector, or generic system register handling, with unclaimed categories falling through to the system path.

The lane provides count and copy helpers for firmware and system identifier lists plus a combined list builder that concatenates core, scalable vector, firmware, and system plus demultiplexed tail entries, supporting a size query when no destination is supplied and advancing the destination by each stage contribution.

Cross file entry points for enumeration and single access include the combined index copier, the single get and set dispatchers, the firmware count plus copy plus single getter, and the system count plus copy plus single getters, each operating on a vCPU with either a user index array or a single register descriptor.

Enumeration and lookup consistently exclude descriptors that offer neither stored backing nor custom user handling and also exclude any descriptor whose optional visibility hook reports hidden for the calling vCPU, so hidden state appears in neither lists nor identifier resolution.

System identifiers combine architecture, width and category markers with five architectural selector fields, while decoding accepts only the 64 bit width, rejects identifiers carrying reserved bits, translates accepted fields into a parameter record, and resolves that record by ordered search over the descriptor table.

Two timer related architectural encodings use dedicated user visible aliases during enumeration, and the reverse translation normalizes those aliases back to canonical system encodings before descriptor lookup, preserving compatibility across identifier families.

Cache size selection state is exposed as a fixed size family of 32 bit demultiplexed identifiers enumerated after normal system registers, and single reads in that family require no unknown bits, require 32 bit width and an in range selector, reporting absence otherwise.

Cache size reads prefer a per vCPU override value when one has been recorded, otherwise they synthesize a conservative value from the smallest line size reported by sanitized feature state, with geometry cleared to a single set and way so guest set way maintenance traps stay minimal.

Scalable vector state is listed with a vector length bitmap pseudo register first followed by per slice groups of vector, predicate and first fault registers, and single reads require vector support plus a finalized configuration, mapping architectural identifiers to offsets in saved state with truncation to the active length and zero fill of any remainder.

The vector length pseudo register is presented as a fixed word array where each length up to the vCPU maximum that is also available on the host sets one bit selected by word index and bit mask derived from the length offset, with all other bits cleared.

Core access interprets identifier low bits as an offset into a mixed width general file viewed in 32 bit units, rejects offsets or offset plus width combinations beyond the file extent or whose requested width mismatches the expected width for that offset, and routes general, stack, program counter, status, privileged and banked exception state and floating point file ranges to separate context storage.

Firmware reads serve a fixed set containing version, three speculation workaround levels derived from host mitigation state with suppression of one workaround when a hardware feature is present, and four feature bitmap words sourced from VM wide storage, reporting absence for other identifiers.

Every path that stores identifiers or values into user memory propagates a fault indication when the store fails, aborting the current enumeration or single access without advancing counts beyond the failure point.

Register identifiers distinguish core, firmware, firmware feature bitmap, scalable vector, system and demultiplexed families through category bits alongside architecture and size markers, with system encodings carrying five selector fields, demultiplexed cache entries carrying selector values, and dedicated constants for timer aliases and vector length state.

The fragments reveal three logical records: a descriptor carrying a storage index, optional custom user handlers, an optional visibility hook and five selector fields; a decoded parameter record carrying those five selectors; and a vector slice mapping carrying a kernel offset, a valid byte count and a pad byte count for user fill.
